title: Beyond Chain-of-Thought: A Survey of Chain-of-X Paradigms for LLMs
best_for_zh: 已了解思维链、希望认识其扩展形式和适用任务的读者。
one_line: A COLING 2025 survey that classifies Chain-of-X methods by their intermediate nodes and their application tasks.
从中间节点类型和应用任务两条线系统整理 Chain-of-X 方法。
why: It helps readers distinguish a chain's representation from the task for which that chain is used.
inclusion_reason: An accepted COLING survey that broadens Chain-of-Thought into a clear vocabulary for different intermediate structures and uses.

title: Problem
问题
html: Chain-of-Thought established the idea that a language model can work through intermediate steps, but later work uses many intermediate components rather than only natural-language thoughts. The authors call this broader family Chain-of-X. It had become hard to compare because papers use different kinds of chain nodes and apply them to different tasks, while similar names can conceal very different designs. The survey therefore helps readers avoid treating a fashionable label as an explanation of mechanism. This COLING 2025 paper is a comprehensive survey, not a new prompting method, model, or data release. Its practical problem is therefore one of orientation: before adopting a chained design, a reader needs to know what each intermediate item represents, what task it supports, and whether the reported benefit belongs to the chain itself or to the surrounding system.

思维链说明了语言模型可以通过中间步骤工作，但后续工作使用的中间组件并不只有自然语言“思考”。作者将这个更宽的方法家族称为 Chain-of-X。由于论文采用不同类型的链节点、服务不同任务，且相近名称可能掩盖完全不同的设计，这些方法已经变得难以比较。因此，这篇综述帮助读者避免把流行名称误当作机制解释。这篇 COLING 2025 论文是对这一方法族的综合综述，不是新的提示方法、模型或数据发布。它要解决的是读者的定位问题：采用某种链式设计前，应先弄清每个中间项代表什么、它支撑什么任务，以及观察到的收益究竟来自链本身还是来自周边系统。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html: The paper treats the X in Chain-of-X as the key design choice and builds one taxonomy around the type of node used in a chain. A second taxonomy groups methods by application task. Together, they prevent a common confusion: two methods may both be sequential, yet differ fundamentally in what each intermediate item represents or in what end task the chain serves. For a reader, this produces a simple comparison frame. First identify the node semantics: is the chain carrying thoughts, actions, code, retrieved material, plans, or another structure? Then identify the application and final output. Only after those two questions are answered does it make sense to compare prompting, cost, transparency, or accuracy across papers. The framework also makes missing descriptions visible: a paper that cannot state its node semantics is difficult to evaluate precisely.

论文把 Chain-of-X 中的 X 视为关键设计选择，并按链节点的类型建立第一套分类；第二套分类按应用任务整理方法。两者合在一起能避免一个常见混淆：两种方法都可能是顺序生成，但每个中间项表示的内容以及最终服务的任务可能根本不同。对读者而言，这给出一个直接的比较框架。先确定节点语义：链中承载的是想法、动作、代码、检索材料、计划，还是其他结构？再确定应用任务和最终输出。只有回答完这两个问题，才适合比较提示方式、成本、可解释性或准确率。这个框架也会暴露描述缺口：若论文无法说清节点语义，就难以进行精确评估。

title: Method
方法
html: Its method is a literature review. It first gives background on Chain-of-Thought, defines Chain-of-X as a broader sequential pattern, and then organizes existing methods by node types and tasks before discussing findings and future directions. The recurring object is a chain: a prompt, one or more intermediate nodes, and a final output, with the node semantics determined by the specific method. The survey is useful as a reading procedure as well as a taxonomy. When examining a cited primary paper, record the input, the unit repeated in the chain, how one unit leads to the next, and the final task output. That schema exposes whether two apparently related methods actually share a mechanism or merely share sequential formatting. It also identifies where an implementation needs a generator, an executor, a checker, or no additional component at all.

论文的方法是文献综述。它先介绍思维链背景，将 Chain-of-X 定义为更广泛的顺序模式，再按节点类型和任务整理现有方法，最后讨论发现与未来方向。反复出现的对象是一条链：提示词、一个或多个中间节点和最终输出；节点的具体含义由方法决定。这套综述也可作为阅读程序。阅读被引用的原始论文时，记录输入、链中重复出现的单位、一个单位如何导向下一个单位，以及最终任务输出。这样的结构化记录能看出两个看似相近的方法是否真的共享机制，还是仅仅采用了相同的顺序呈现形式。它还可看出实现中是否需要生成器、执行器、检查器，或根本不需要额外组件。

title: Evidence
证据
html: The evidence is the paper's collection and organization of existing Chain-of-X work. Its official abstract states that it reviews methods in different contexts, provides the two taxonomies, and discusses findings and implications. The survey does not claim that every chain design improves every task; performance evidence remains attached to the original method and evaluation setting. This matters when using the card as evidence. A category tells readers how to locate comparable work, not that all members have identical performance. Check the cited paper for the base model, prompt or training setting, task metric, and any tool or external information used. A gain may reflect the node representation, but it may also reflect additional context, search, or evaluation choices. This is particularly important when a chain is paired with tools: the outcome may depend on tool interaction rather than textual decomposition alone.

论文的证据来自对既有 Chain-of-X 工作的收集和组织。官方摘要说明，它回顾不同情境下的方法，给出两套分类，并讨论已有发现和含义。综述并未声称每种链设计都会提升每项任务；性能证据仍属于具体方法及其原始评测设置。把这张卡当作证据时尤其需要注意：一个类别告诉读者如何找到可比较的工作，并不意味着同类方法拥有相同表现。应回到被引用论文核对基础模型、提示或训练条件、任务指标，以及是否使用工具或外部信息。性能提升可能来自节点表示，也可能来自额外上下文、搜索或评测选择。链与工具配合时尤其如此：观察到的结果可能依赖工具交互，而不只是文本分解。

title: Novelty
新意
html: The survey's new contribution is its joint view of components and tasks. Earlier discussions often begin and end with CoT, whereas this paper treats CoT as one influential starting point for a broader family. Its value is conceptual: when a paper introduces a new “chain,” readers can ask both what the nodes are and why this task needs them. The contribution is not a common benchmark, a new training recipe, or a proof that one chain type is best. Instead, it supplies vocabulary that makes novelty claims more precise. A new method may change the node type, the transition between nodes, the task application, or only the presentation. Readers should identify which of these actually changes before treating a named variant as a distinct reasoning advance.

综述的新贡献是把组件和任务放在一起看。以往讨论常从 CoT 开始也止于 CoT，而本文将 CoT 视为更大方法族的一个重要起点。它的价值主要在概念层面：遇到一个新的“链”时，读者可以同时追问节点是什么，以及该任务为什么需要这种节点。它并未提供统一基准、新训练配方，也没有证明某类链必然最好；它提供的是让新颖性说法更精确的词汇。一种新方法可能改变节点类型、节点间转移、应用任务，或仅仅改变展示形式。读者应先辨别真正变化的是哪一项，再把带有新名字的变体视为独立的推理进展。

title: Limitations
局限
html: The taxonomy describes a heterogeneous field, so it is not a controlled experiment that isolates one universal effect of chaining. A chain can be useful as a representation, a prompt, a tool interface, or a planning device, and these uses should not be collapsed into one claim about reasoning ability. Names are also an unreliable shortcut: a method may contain a chain without exposing useful intermediate information, and an apparently different method may share the same underlying decomposition. For implementation details, data, and evaluation protocols, consult the primary papers named in the relevant category. Do not infer reproducibility, faithfulness of explanations, or transfer across tasks from the survey alone; those depend on the individual system and its measurements.

这套分类描述的是异质领域，并不是隔离某种通用链效果的对照实验。一条链可以是表示形式、提示方式、工具接口或规划工具，这些用途不应被压缩成关于推理能力的单一结论。名称同样不是可靠捷径：某方法可能有链却没有暴露有用的中间信息，表面不同的方法也可能共享同一分解方式。若需实现细节、数据或评测协议，应查阅相应类别中的原始论文。不要只凭综述推断可复现性、解释是否忠实，或结果能否迁移到其他任务；这些结论取决于各个系统及其测量方式。

title: Usefulness
用途
html: Use this paper when you need to choose or explain an intermediate structure in an LLM system. Start with the node taxonomy to find methods that use a compatible representation, then use the task taxonomy to see how that representation has been applied. It is especially helpful for avoiding superficial comparisons based only on names such as “chain,” “thought,” or “agent.” For a literature review, make a small table with one row per candidate method: node type, transition mechanism, task, output, and evidence available. For system design, use the same table to decide whether an intermediate structure is needed for control, tool interaction, decomposition, or communication. The survey helps formulate the choice, but primary experiments are still needed to choose a method.

当需要为语言模型系统选择或解释中间结构时，可以使用这篇论文。先按节点分类寻找表示形式相近的方法，再按任务分类了解这种表示形式被如何使用。它尤其适合避免只凭“chain”“thought”或“agent”等名称做表面比较。做文献综述时，可以为每个候选方法建立一行记录：节点类型、转移机制、任务、输出和已有证据。做系统设计时，也可用同一张表判断中间结构是为了控制、工具交互、任务分解还是沟通。本文帮助把选择说清楚，但真正选定方法仍需依靠原始实验。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html: Read the definition of Chain-of-X and the node taxonomy before browsing the application examples. For any cited method, write a short schema for one chain item and a short sentence for the task objective; this makes the two taxonomies operational. Next, ask what produces each node, what consumes it, and whether it is checked, executed, or simply shown to the model. These details distinguish a reasoning trace from an action sequence, a retrieval sequence, or an output format. The final discussion is useful for recognizing where a sequential design is genuinely necessary and where it mainly changes the presentation of intermediate work. Keep conclusions modest when the underlying studies use different tasks, models, or budgets.

建议先读 Chain-of-X 的定义和节点分类，再浏览应用例子。对于任意被引用方法，写下一个链节点的简短结构和一句任务目标，这样两套分类才能真正用起来。接着问：每个节点由什么产生、被什么消费，它是被检查、执行，还是只展示给模型？这些细节能区分推理轨迹、动作序列、检索序列和输出格式。最后的讨论有助于判断顺序设计何时确有必要，何时主要只是改变了中间工作的呈现形式。底层研究若使用不同任务、模型或计算预算，结论就应保持克制。
